AGGREGATE reads - the Operations dashboard's netted availableStock, consumption and technician-volume rollups, and getInventoryAnalytics - cannot, because a page of inputs yields a false total. Only the first group is unblocked by the list runtime; the second needs an authoritative aggregate and is tracked under X-INVENTORY-ANALYTICS-AGGREGATE. 'Generalize the cursor prior art' does NOT mean writing a second paging helper: the list query core already IS that generalization, and a board needs a BOUNDED READ without needing a GRID. The AGGREGATE reads are NOT, and must not be bounded as if they were: netting a total over a page produces an arithmetically false figure under a name implying a complete one, which is worse than an honest failure. entries.title: Index derivation across filter COMBINATIONS
entries.nextAction: Merged; three accounts composites declared and pending deploy
entries.notes: requiredIndexes() emits ONE combined index for all declared filters plus the sort. Firestore does not serve a query filtering on a subset from that index, so a list declaring two independent filters really demands several indexes. It also emits `order` for every filter field, which is wrong for array-contains - that needs arrayConfig CONTAINS. This is why the Customers relationship facet is deferred: its honest query is array-contains beside an ordering, and the derivation cannot yet state the index it needs. Until this exists, a definition may declare at most one filter without the gate understating what the backend must provide. DELIVERED (#1139): one index per combination, arrayConfig for array operators, no composite demanded for the unfiltered single-field-ordered query (Firestore's automatic index serves it), and MAX_DECLARED_FILTERS=4 as a validation failure since the set is exponential in the optional filters. The Customers relationship facet was restored in the same PR - it had been deferred precisely because this derivation could not state the index it needed. Single-select, not the old multi-select: Firestore permits one array filter per query, so an intersection would promise a query no declared index serves.

entries.title: Governed Account search
entries.nextAction: Merged. Case-insensitive and substring search remain named gaps, not silent ones.
entries.notes: The accounts search provider filtered an array the whole-collection subscription supplied, so removing that subscription removed its only possible input. Handing it a page would return 'no results' for customers that exist - a search box that silently finds nothing is worse than none, because it answers. Removed from /customers in #1138 and recorded here. MERGED (#1177): a bounded Firestore PREFIX range on name, not a client-side filter. Firestore has no substring or full-text index, so prefix is the only honest primitive on an indexed string field - 'corp' will not find 'Anchor Corp', every user-facing string says 'starts with' rather than an unqualified 'search', and case sensitivity is NAMED as a gap. Fixing either needs a normalized field on the write path or an external index, both out of scope and both recorded rather than faked. No composite index required: a single range filter on the field it orders by uses the automatic single-field index, verified rather than assumed. INTEGRATION CORRECTION: the lane reported no registration pending, but its new node:test suite was in no workflow and no npm script and would never have run - a new test file does not feel like a shared-resource edit, which is exactly why the CI-matrix rule exists.

entries.title: Field Architecture v2
entries.nextAction: Gate cleared. Mass entity definition may resume.
entries.notes: v1 is NOT superseded - it remains the read/query/render contract and every merged definition stays valid. What v1 must not be is final: it has one identity (id), no notion of a derived value, and a type list that treats every number alike. Scope: label vs systemName (immutable machine identity, NOT vendor 'API Name'); field classes STANDARD/SYSTEM/CUSTOM/DERIVED with DERIVED split into FORMULA/LOOKUP/ROLLUP/PROJECTION and NOT collapsed into one calculated-field concept; explicit numeric semantics incl. percentage storage and the rule that formatting never changes an authoritative value; a constrained validated expression vocabulary with no executable metadata; dependency graph by systemName with circular rejection and cross-entity authority that cannot become an authorization bypass; VIRTUAL/MATERIALIZED/AGGREGATE queryability where displayable does not imply filterable; the full behavior contract through deprecation; an EOS-native standard vocabulary that standardizes MEANING without forcing every entity to carry every field; storage separation so systemName is never assumed to be the Firestore path; and a custom-field SEAM, not the custom-field product. Specification merged as 98d15344 (docs/specifications/field-architecture-v2.md, DECISIONS #103). The GATE itself - the design work - is what remains READY. IMPLEMENTED ADDITIVELY (#1147, 379ef835) under src/metadata/v2/ - identity, numeric, formula and fieldDefinitionV2 modules with 32 invariant tests. All eleven clearing conditions are met: durable field identity, systemName semantics, field classes, derived-field types, numeric/rounding semantics, dependency rules, authority semantics, queryability distinctions, migration compatibility, the custom-field seam, and tests that enforce the architecture. The final condition - compatibility - is PROVEN against the two real merged definitions rather than fixtures: 18 tests assert Account and Work Order map into v2 with systemName, label, operators and enum vocabulary (including the NUMERIC one) surviving unchanged, and every field recording UNKNOWN_MUTABILITY and UNKNOWN_WRITE_CAPABILITY rather than inventing an answer.

entries.title: Record provenance platform invariant
entries.nextAction: Merged. The origin seam (createdVia/initiatedBy/sourceExecutionId) awaits reconciliation with the audit event architecture before anything writes it.
entries.notes: Server-authoritative: no writeCapability, because a client-supplied timestamp or actor is a CLAIM - any caller who can write the record can write the claim. Append-only records get two fields, not four: emitting updatedAt on an issued invoice implies a mutation path that must not exist. Synonyms (creationDate, lastModified) are REJECTED - legacy storage is handled with storagePath, never a second name in the standard vocabulary. Exemptions for caches/locks/transient state require a stated reason, so an exemption is a decision rather than a gap. Deliberately does NOT duplicate the audit event architecture: provenance is current state, audit is each material mutation, and reconstructing history from updatedBy makes the last writer look like the only writer.

entries.title: Unified EOS query model (shared dependency)
entries.nextAction: Merged. Automation v1, EQL v1 and Bulk Data v1 are unblocked; migrating the list runtime onto the AST is a separate slice.
entries.notes: RECORDED AS A SHARED DEPENDENCY so it is not rediscovered independently by Lists, Reports, Automation, EQL and AI. List filters, saved views, the report builder, automation conditions, EQL, AI-generated queries and the admin visual builder converge on ONE governed query AST, then one pipeline: metadata validation, authority validation, queryability validation, index validation, planner, governed execution. Independent query semantics per feature is how six subsystems end up disagreeing about what a filter means. Must ABSORB the existing governed report creator rather than run beside it, and must NOT collapse the board-scope contract into list pagination - a board returns a complete working set or admits it cannot, which is a different promise from a page. BUILT: makeQuery/comparison/group/traversal AST plus validateAgainstMetadata -> validateAuthority -> validateQueryability, stopping at the first refusal. Stage ORDER is deliberate: reporting a denial for a field that does not exist tells a caller something false about their access, and reporting a missing index for an unauthorized query leaks the shape of data they cannot see. A field a viewer may not READ cannot be FILTERED on either, because a predicate over a hidden field leaks its values by binary search. Traversal authority is the RELATED entity, not this one. An empty IN is REFUSED rather than resolved by whichever backend runs it - ambiguous by convention, and six consumers guessing separately is what this model prevents. completeness PAGE/COMPLETE/AGGREGATE keeps the board promise distinct from list paging rather than collapsing it.

entries.title: Automation Architecture v1
entries.nextAction: Design after the unified query model - automation CONDITIONS are queries
entries.notes: Visual flow builder to declarative model to governed execution engine. WHEN/IF/THEN over REGISTERED actions only. Core invariant: admins may COMPOSE approved business capabilities; automation may not INVENT executable authority - an engine that could write arbitrary fields is a database backdoor with a friendly interface. No JavaScript, Python, SQL writes, eval or executable metadata reaches an administrator. Operability is part of v1 rather than a later hardening pass: dry-run, execution audit, correlation identity, loop and recursion prevention, retry/idempotency, draft/active lifecycle, versioning. The canonical incident is A changes status triggering B changing status triggering A, and causality is cheaper to design than to diagnose.

entries.title: EQL / Governed Query Architecture v1
entries.nextAction: Design the surface syntax AFTER the shared query model it compiles into
entries.notes: SQL-INSPIRED because those concepts are already understood by developers, analysts, admins, BI users and AI - but claiming NO ANSI compatibility, exposing no Firestore, and never implying relational joins EOS cannot execute honestly. References stable systemNames so a label change cannot break a query. Relationships traversed by registered name, never by reconstructing storage join predicates. READ-ORIENTED: no UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT/DROP/ALTER - bulk modification is query, preview scope, choose a registered governed action, validate authority, execute, audit. AI gets no bypass: AI-generated queries pass the same validation as human-authored ones, which is the point of having one contract.

entries.title: Bulk Data Architecture v1 (import + export)
entries.nextAction: Design after the query model - an export IS a governed query with a different sink
entries.notes: Core invariant: BULK CHANGES SCALE, NOT AUTHORITY - a bulk operation cannot do what its initiating actor could not do one record at a time. Identity uses recordId, business reference or approved alternateKey; NEVER a mutable human label. 0 matches create-if-permitted, 1 match update, more than 1 is an INTEGRITY FAILURE and never a guess. Dry run mutates nothing. EXPORT AUTHORITY IS A HARD BOUNDARY: if a user may read 4,200 records and 8 fields, Export All means all within THEIR authorized scope - not 4,201 records, not a ninth field - and the server-side job enforces it, because UI hiding is not enforcement. Export modes are distinct (human/update/integration/template/audit) and display values are not machine values, so a round-trip cannot corrupt an authoritative value. Every export produces an immutable audit record including the EFFECTIVE authorized scope, and export authority may never exceed read authority though policy may later make it stricter.

entries.title: Admin metadata configuration / page designer
entries.nextAction: Design after entities are defined - there is nothing to configure until there is metadata to configure
entries.notes: Admins configure through BUSINESS concepts, not Firestore/React/JSON/source. Field creation exposes friendly choices that EOS translates into the governed contract; systemName is proposed from the label, correctable before creation, stable after. Semantic documentation (purpose, businessMeaning, ownerDomain, sourceOfTruth) is OPTIONAL - requiring it to create a simple field produces documentation written to satisfy a validator. Page metadata REQUESTS presentation and never grants authority: editable applies only if the field is updateable AND the viewer holds write authority AND the command permits it AND lifecycle state allows it. OPERATIONAL pages are protected - layout flexibility may not remove Lifecycle/Readiness/Blockers/Next Actions, because placement flexibility and composition invariants are separate concerns and only one is negotiable. Preview must evaluate REAL governed authority; a preview with its own permission model reports what the builder thinks rather than what the platform will do. Publication must fail where the backend cannot honestly support the declared behavior.

entries.title: Contact write paths do not agree on provenance
entries.nextAction: Future writes converged. Historical backfill remains a separate decision requiring evidence.
entries.notes: Found while defining the Contact entity. createContact writes NEITHER timestamp; the CSV importer writes createdAt/updatedAt and no actor; only the sandbox seed writes createdBy/updatedBy. The provenance invariant says every durable business record carries createdAt/createdBy, and contacts are durable business records. The metadata definition deliberately does NOT declare the fields, because declaring them would assert data absent from most existing documents - the remediation is a write-path change plus a backfill decision, not a metadata claim. Backfilling historical documents is a data question and may be protected. FUTURE-WRITE CONVERGENCE MERGED (#1157, c97694a7): all three paths now write the four fields, and updateContact never rewrites createdAt/createdBy. Reuses the existing auth.currentUser actor pattern rather than inventing a resolution path. HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT IS NOT: Contact writes are client-direct, so these values are client-supplied CLAIMS rather than server-authoritative provenance - any caller able to write a Contact can write them. The change converges the SHAPE, not the trust model; making them authoritative means moving Contact writes behind a trusted command, which is a separate unauthorized decision. No historical rows were touched. Also closed a gap found in passing: contacts.js and contactImport.js had NO CI coverage at all.

Sales Order gets a real immutable business reference, SO-YYYY-######, joining the approved family beside WO- and OPP-. salesOrderNumber is STANDARD/STRING/immutable/unique; alternateKey is evaluated separately rather than assumed from uniqueness. NUMBERING MERGED (#1156, 0f797a01): salesOrderNumber is allocated inside the caller's transaction on BOTH creation paths, from a per-year counter distinct from the opportunity and work-order counters so the sequences never interact. Server-authoritative by construction - the pure builder never carries the field, so there is nothing for a client value to override - and immutable by construction rather than by a runtime guard, verified by confirming no transition or update path writes it. Deliberately mirrors opportunityNumbering.ts rather than reinventing the concurrency story.

entries.title: Equipment stores epoch-number timestamps and no actor
entries.nextAction: Blocked on a Rules change: equipmentWritableKeys/equipmentEditableKeys must admit createdBy/updatedBy before any client can write them.
governing: Owner Sales Order identity ruling section 12
entries.notes: Found while scouting Equipment for definition. The equipment collection carries createdAt/updatedAt as NUMBERS (epoch millis, per the Rules type check) and has NO createdBy/updatedBy at all - unlike parts and equipment_models, which carry the full four as Firestore Timestamps. Two rules apply. First, determine the actual stored semantics before presenting anything: reinterpreting an epoch number as a Timestamp to match the standard presentation would misread the data rather than describe it. Second, if legacy storage must stay compatible, that is exactly what the systemName/storagePath separation is for - the standard vocabulary keeps its names and the mapping absorbs the difference. Historical actor backfill requires evidence; UNKNOWN is preferable to an invented actor. LANE DISPATCHED at base 80302959, following the Contact convergence (#1157) as precedent: future writes only, no backfill, same actor mechanism, and timestamps STAY epoch-millis numbers because firestore.rules asserts `is number` and Rules are outside the lane's scope. The brief requires checking equipmentWritableKeys() FIRST: if that allowlist is strict, adding createdBy/updatedBy would be REJECTED at write time, and the correct outcome is a reported blocker rather than code that cannot work. Rules deployment is a protected action. LANE STOPPED CORRECTLY WITHOUT WRITING CODE. The brief required checking the Rules allowlist BEFORE implementing, and the check failed: unlike Contact - whose Rules use no field allowlist, which is why that convergence worked - equipment's Rules fail closed on any key nobody has thought of yet. That anti-injection design is correct and is exactly what blocks this. Writing the client change anyway would have produced code that cannot function and would have broken every equipment write the moment it shipped. The implementation SHAPE is recorded for whoever picks this up once Rules are amended: wrap equipmentStore in equipmentRepository.js so the actor is merged at the same point makeCollectionStore already stamps createdAt, which keeps createdBy off update naturally and leaves the pure payload builders in equipmentWrites.js firebase-free.

entries.title: Shared-resource ownership in the writer-lane model
entries.nextAction: Merged: canDispatch fails closed on contention; registrationGaps checks both directions.
entries.notes: PRINCIPLE RECORDED in agent-isolation-execution-rule.md: parallelize disjoint implementation, serialize shared registration and integration. A central registry edited by five agents is not five-way parallelism - it is five writers contending on one resource. The CODE half remains: lanes declare sharedResources beside writeScope; a shared resource has at most one active owner; dispatch fails closed on collision; logical resources (METADATA_REGISTRATION, INDEX_DECLARATIONS, WORKFLOW_METADATA_TESTS) cover families spanning several files; and a lock is released only after useful work is preserved, never because an agent says it finished. Registration-completeness checks should prefer SET EQUALITY over one-way containment, since an omitted or extra item is a coverage defect in both directions. Evidence it is needed: the Sales Order definition lane and the header lane were dispatched as disjoint and both were routed toward the same workflow and index registration files; they happened not to collide because the header lane needed no new test file. MERGED (#1165): lanes declare writeScope and sharedResources, canDispatch FAILS CLOSED when a resource is owned, a MERGED lane releases its claims, undeclaredSharedEdits and outOfScopeFiles detect what isolation cannot prevent, and registrationGaps reports missing AND orphaned because a one-way check would pass while half a batch was invisible. 27 tests.

entries.title: A background agent outlives its dispatching context; absence of a branch is not death
entries.nextAction: Corrected. Check for running agents before concluding a lane is lost.
entries.notes: CORRECTED RECORD. This entry originally claimed a writer lane had been LOST because its worktree died with the session. That did not happen, and the claim was mine, not an agent's. At resumption I ran ls-remote for the lane's branch, saw nothing, and concluded the work was gone. The agent was simply still RUNNING in the background: it pushed 54cb84e9 minutes later, and its completion notification arrived after I had already re-dispatched a replacement. Nothing was lost; I checked too early and inferred death from a single point-in-time absence. The cost was a duplicated lane -- the replacement independently reached the same conclusions, found the pushed branch when its own push was rejected non-fast-forward, correctly refused to overwrite superior work, and reported instead. THE REAL LESSON: a background agent can outlive the context that dispatched it, so 'no branch on origin' is evidence of nothing on its own. Check whether the lane is still running before concluding loss, and prefer waiting to re-dispatching. The push-before-handoff practice recorded as rule 9a remains sound guidance on its own merits, but it was NOT earned by this incident, and the rule now says so.

entries.title: Location entity + list definition (leaf lane)
entries.nextAction: Merged and registered via the integration lane.

entries.title: Account page: Locations section and Commercial Profile fields
entries.nextAction: Both gaps closed. Wiring is the remaining lane.
entries.notes: Recorded rather than filled by the page lane, because declaring either would have been a page promising data the entity cannot supply. Locations needs an account.locations relationship on account.js plus a RELATED list - the Location leaf could not add the edge and said so. Commercial Profile and Notes/Identifiers render real fields (owner, currency, payment terms, tax status, customerNumber, erpId) that accountEntity does not declare at all: it carries only name, status, relationshipTypes, updatedAt and tags. Both are entity work first, page work second. ENTITY HALF MERGED (#1185, c6bfb148): twelve fields plus the account.locations edge. THE GOVERNED-FIELD FINDING is the part to remember - account.governedField.write gates WRITE for paymentTerms and taxStatus, while the account document's READ gate is uniformly isAdminOrDispatcher() for the whole record. v1's readCapability models READ authority and has NO writeCapability concept, so declaring the governed id as a readCapability would have asserted a read restriction that does not exist. Neither field declares one, and the gap is pinned by a comment AND a test rather than guessed either way - Field Architecture v2 defines writeCapability, and this is exactly the seam it exists for. Six accountOwner sub-fields were deliberately left undeclared: they are stored, but resolveOwnerIdentity re-resolves the CURRENT name live rather than reading the snapshot, so declaring them would describe the schema rather than the system. PAGE HALF MERGED (#1187, f18b0e83). The RELATED locations list became declarable only because the account.locations edge landed first - a RELATED list's parent relationship must REACH the listed entity, which is why location.js had shipped INDEX-only. Sections were matched against AccountDetail field by field IN RENDER ORDER rather than grouped by judgement, and the SIDE ordering was confirmed against the JSX. TWO DELIBERATE CAPABILITY ABSENCES, both cited: locations declares none because locationEntity.readCapability is null, and Commercial Profile declares none because account.governedField.write gates WRITE only - a section-level READ capability would have contradicted the entity it renders. Declaring a stricter-looking gate would have been the easy move and the wrong one.

entries.title: Upgrade locationId from STRING to REFERENCE on equipment and salesOrder
entries.nextAction: Merged. Index demands verified unchanged and pinned by test.
entries.notes: Both files declared locationId as a plain STRING because no location entity was registered, and both said so in comments. That entity now exists. Deliberately NOT done in the integration lane: changing a field's TYPE is on the integrator's forbidden list, and a file comment inviting the change does not convert a semantic edit into a mechanical one. It belongs to a focused lane over those two files. MERGED (#1183, d6e29a5d). The index-demand check was the real safeguard rather than the type change itself: a REFERENCE stays display-only unless someone declares it filterable, so the risk is a LATER edit quietly turning a display reference into a queryable one and adding index cost nobody reviewed. requiredIndexes() was compared before and after, found byte-identical, and pinned by a test asserting no index field path names locationId - verified independently at the controller before acceptance. Rules behaviour was described accurately rather than assumed symmetrical: equipment has a real enforced ownership check, salesOrder has NO equivalent cross-check and stores locationId as string|null.

entries.title: Wire AccountDetail onto the Account record PageDefinition
entries.nextAction: Partial wiring merged. Related lists and field groups need renderer support first.
entries.notes: The definition exists and validates; AccountDetail.jsx is untouched. Wiring needs five component ids registered in componentRegistry - accountHealthStrip, accountFinancialsSection, accountActivityAndNotesSection, accountServiceActivity, accountAttentionSection - since a definition may only name a REGISTERED component id, never a function. The visibility path must keep failing closed: pageRuntime applies caller-supplied decisions and an empty map hides every gated section rather than revealing it. DISPATCHED at f18b0e83. The brief forbids inventing a resolver or passing a permissive default: an empty decision map HIDING sections is correct fail-closed behaviour, while an all-true map is a security defect. If no suitable client-side resolver exists the lane must STOP and report rather than substitute one. It may also choose partial wiring over a full swap - a partial honest wiring beats a full one that silently changes what a user sees. MERGED (#1191, ac1a979f) as a PARTIAL wiring, and the reason is the valuable part. All five component ids are registered; three are wired live. Account Attention was registered, tested, and then DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED: it is the only section in the SIDE region, so when finance.read denies, MetadataRecordPage's 'zero visible sections means DENIED' rule would replace the component's graceful per-source degradation with a page-level failure state. An existing fail-closed test caught that during wiring and the lane reverted rather than shipping it. The capability resolver composes the SANCTIONED primitives that useReportCapabilities and useOpportunityCapabilities already use, requesting exactly the ids declaredPageCapabilities returns rather than a hand-typed list, and denying everything while loading, signed out or erroring. One regression was found and fixed rather than shipped: metadata-rendered sections had lost their 16px gap because each region is now its own wrapper, so a metadata-rendered page would have been recognisable by its spacing.

entries.title: Warehouse + Supplier entity definitions
entries.nextAction: Merged and registered. Two composites declared and pending deploy.
entries.notes: THE TWO ENTITIES TOOK OPPOSITE POSITIONS ON THE SAME QUESTION, correctly. Warehouse does NOT declare its governed provenance pack: the schema exists as a TypeScript type, but both producers describe themselves as production-inert with no caller and are not exported from the functions index, so declaring eight fields no live write path produces would describe an intention rather than the system. Supplier DOES declare its pack, because supplierMasterCommands is a real exported write path - the same posture part.js takes. Supplier is also the FIRST entity here whose provenance is genuine Firestore Timestamps rather than epoch millis, and it says so rather than quietly matching the others. Same question, different answers, because the evidence differs. TWO REFUSALS: warehouse.location stays a plain STRING and is explicitly NOT a REFERENCE to the registered `location` entity - it is free text about a building, and the shared word would have made a REFERENCE a plausible-looking lie. supplier.vendorNumber stays an ordinary optional STRING rather than a referenceField, since promoting an unenforced non-unique field licenses the document-id fallback #106 forbids. OPEN EDGES recorded rather than invented: warehouse has no outbound edges because stock_locations, transfer_orders and mobile_locations all carry a warehouseId but none has a registered entity to own the edge; supplier.partSupplierItems is a real edge waiting on a partSupplierItem entity that does not exist.

entries.title: MetadataRecordPage: related-list wiring, FIELD_GROUP renderer, single-section DENIED
entries.nextAction: All three gaps closed. Account completion wiring dispatched.
entries.notes: Found by wiring a real page rather than by review. (1) No listResolver/listRenderer wiring exists, so RELATED_LIST sections cannot render through the metadata path yet - four Account sections wait on it. (2) There is no generic FIELD_GROUP renderer, so a componentId-less FIELD_GROUP renders EMPTY rather than failing loudly, which is the worse of the two failure modes. (3) The 'zero visible sections means DENIED' rule is right for a whole page but wrong for a REGION containing one gated section: it converts a component's graceful per-source degradation into a page-level denial. The Attention section is the concrete case and is why it stayed hand-rendered. DISPATCHED at ef6baee5. The brief prefers a real FIELD_GROUP renderer over a louder failure message where one can be built honestly - a page that CAN render a field group is worth more than one that reports it cannot - while keeping the listRenderer INJECTION POINT so a caller can still supply its own and the renderer stays testable. The region-granularity fix must preserve the hidden-by-access versus no-sections-configured distinction, which is correct and already tested. Any existing test pinning the old region-level denial encoded the defect and gets its invariant corrected rather than the fix weakened. MERGED (#1194, 27b109bb). FIELD_GROUP renders generically, reusing cellValue from listPresentation rather than re-deriving enum handling - so a machine value cannot reach a user through this path while the list path resolves it. RELATED_LIST gained a default binding built on the same three primitives useMetadataList uses, and the lane deliberately did NOT reuse that hook: its request shape never forwards parentId/relationships, so reusing it would have produced a related list quietly showing EVERY record of the target entity. GAP 3 WAS SHARPER THAN IT LOOKED: a single-section, single-region definition is structurally IDENTICAL whether it is the whole page or a fragment of a hand-composed one, so the renderer cannot infer which and guessing is wrong for the other case. An `embedded` prop makes the caller state it. The lane also checked whether an existing test had encoded the old behaviour, found none had, and said so - worth recording because the opposite has been true four times here.

entries.title: Transfer Order + Manufacturer definitions (leaf lane)

Manufacturer stores a normalizedName, which is a matching KEY and not a display value - presenting it as one would be the same class of error as showing a document id. And the warehouse entity now exists, so a transfer order's from/to warehouse fields MAY honestly be REFERENCEs, but only after the real field names are verified rather than assumed. part.js still declares primaryManufacturerId as a plain STRING; that upgrade belongs to a separate lane, not to this one. SPLIT AT INTEGRATION. Manufacturer merged (#1196, ed448c75): CALLABLE read behind inventory.catalog.read; normalizedName declared AND noted as having ZERO consumers anywhere - a write-time artifact rather than a display value, unlike supplier's normalizedKey which at least gates dedup detection; all four provenance fields stored and repository-enforced but NOT returned by the current projection, the same honesty pattern salesOrder used for its undelivered number. Transfer Order was NOT merged - see X-TRANSFER-ORDER-NO-REFERENCE.

entries.title: Complete the Account page wiring now the renderer supports it
entries.nextAction: No section newly wired. Three prerequisites identified and recorded.
entries.notes: Dispatched at 27b109bb. The standing constraint is unchanged and was right the first time: if any section renders WORSE through metadata - wrong data, lost scoping, lost graceful degradation, changed layout - it stays hand-rendered and gets reported. Partial and honest beats complete and wrong. The specific risk here is an UNSCOPED related list: one showing every contact in the system would be far worse than the hand-rendered version it replaced, so scoping must be verified rather than assumed from the binding existing. OUTCOME: NO SECTION WAS NEWLY WIRED (#1198, f42491de), and that is the correct result. Closing the three renderer gaps made every remaining section mechanically renderable; it did not make any of them SAFE. Each was checked against what it would REPLACE rather than against whether the renderer could now produce some output, and all six render measurably worse. What landed is the evidence plus two tests locking the findings in, so the next lane does not re-derive them.

entries.title: Transfer Order has no identity of either kind

It records the gap honestly and pins it with a test asserting exactly one validation problem - but merging a definition that fails its own contract would weaken the contract by demonstrating it can be carried broken. THE PRECEDENT IS EXACT: X-SALES-ORDER-NO-REFERENCE blocked the Sales Order definition for this same condition, and Sales Order waited for a governed SO-YYYY-###### before its definition landed. Inventing a transfer numbering scheme is the same business decision this program already ruled is not a leaf's to make. The authored file is preserved on feat/transfer-manufacturer-definitions and can be merged unchanged once the decision exists.

entries.title: RELATED_LIST cannot read a CALLABLE-readVia entity
entries.nextAction: Merged. Opportunities and Sales Orders are now wirable; that lane is dispatched.
entries.notes: THE STRUCTURAL BLOCKER on page wiring. The default RELATED_LIST binding is built on fetchPage, which always issues a direct client getDocs -- but opportunity and salesOrder declare readVia CALLABLE, their collections are DENY-ALL in Rules, and real reads happen only through trusted callables. Wiring either today would read a deny-all collection and report EVERY viewer as denied, permanently, even one holding the real capability. The binding ignores a fact the entity explicitly declares. The fix must FAIL LOUDLY for UNKNOWN readVia or a CALLABLE entity with no readCallable, rather than silently falling through to a direct read - that silent fallthrough IS the defect. MERGED (#1200, 6c6480d8). selectListSource routes by readVia; UNKNOWN or CALLABLE with no readCallable short-circuits to unavailable and touches NEITHER source, because the silent fallthrough to a direct read WAS the defect. The scope filter is read generically off the parent-scope filter buildQueryDescriptor always prepends rather than hardcoding accountId, and both callables' existing limit+1 convention feeds the SAME interpretPage the Firestore path uses - two independent truncation rules would eventually disagree. A callable rejection's code is normalized so DENIED stays distinct from UNAVAILABLE without the caller knowing the source. ALSO FIXED, flagged by the lane as pre-existing: the related-list hook computed hasMore correctly and then threw it away, so a capped RELATED section presented its cap as the whole set - the precise failure the presentation model exists to prevent, arriving through the one path that had already worked out the right answer.

entries.title: A section capability cannot express a partially-gated composition
entries.nextAction: None. Adoption is gated on the FieldGroup consumer.
entries.notes: Found by trying to wire Account Attention. The page declares ONE capability for a component composing TWO sources at DIFFERENT authority levels: its AR read is finance.read-gated, its past-due Work Order read is ungated. A section-level requirement can only honour the coarser gate, so wiring it hides the ungated half too. finance.read is catalog-wide active:false, so this is not theoretical - it would blank the panel for every viewer today. The `embedded` prop fixed the region-denial symptom correctly; this is a different problem underneath it, and conflating the two would have shipped a blank panel while believing the fix worked. RESOLVED by capabilityParts: an additive, mutually-exclusive alternative to capabilityRequirement. All parts denied removes the section entirely (unchanged financials/activityAndNotes precedent); some denied keeps the section and attaches visiblePartIds/withheldPartIds/partiallyWithheld so the withholding is FLAGGED rather than silently trimmed; none denied is normal. Additivity proven by a test asserting a single-capability page carries none of the new keys across missing/false/true decisions. Grounded in the real decision feed, and confirmed Account Attention is exactly the recorded case -- finance.read gating a section that composes a finance.read AR read with an UNGATED work-order past-due read.

entries.title: FieldGroup does not honor withheld parts -- capabilityParts must not be adopted on a FIELD_GROUP yet
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: The generic FieldGroup renderer in MetadataRecordPage.jsx renders every id in section.fieldIds unconditionally, so a composed FIELD_GROUP would silently omit withheld fields with no trace -- the exact failure capabilityParts exists to prevent. This is the SAME SHAPE as the stale rowNavigationTo removed in #1207: a declaration no consumer honors is harmless right up until something reads it. Merging #1209 was safe only because NO definition adopts capabilityParts yet (accountPage.js still declares the single finance.read gate). Recorded rather than left to memory: do not migrate accountAttention, or any other FIELD_GROUP, until this lands. Component-path sections need no change -- Section already forwards the resolved section object through. RESOLVED at f013d965. CORRECTION to this entry as originally written: closing this did NOT unblock accountAttention adopting capabilityParts, and the entry should not be read as saying so. AccountAttentionSection is a registered componentId section, and Section() resolves a componentId before FieldGroup is ever reached -- component-path sections already received the resolved section object for free from #1209. What this closed is the GENERIC FIELD_GROUP hole, which was real and genuinely unconsumed. Account Attention's own composition remains a separate decision. Three fail-closed choices were made deliberately: an unclaimed field is withheld rather than shown (default-show would make 'forgot to add this field to the new part' the silent failure mode when composing an existing section; fail-closed makes that same mistake safe); malformed part metadata withholds the ENTIRE section, since the runtime cannot know what a broken declaration would have claimed; and structural validation runs again at render time rather than assuming the definition validator ran.

entries.title: MetadataListGrid has no row actions or focus handoff
entries.nextAction: Wiring Contacts/Locations onto it is a separate lane.
entries.notes: Contacts and Locations are mechanically wirable but would lose Add/Import actions and the post-add keyboard focus handoff to the new row, which MetadataListGrid has no ref hook to reproduce. Losing focus handoff is an ACCESSIBILITY regression, not a cosmetic one. Wiring them would also start a SECOND live read of a query those pages must keep running anyway - the double-read pattern this codebase already tracks as a production bug. RESOLVED. The lane read the hand-written sections before designing and found the entry's premise was imprecise: there are NO per-row edit/delete actions today, only section-level '+ Add' buttons. The real blocker was post-create FOCUS -- AccountDetail.jsx keeps pendingContactFocus state and a row ref, and its own comment says MetadataListGrid exposes no per-row ref. Shipped: rowActions {id,label,onActivate,denied,deniedReason} resolved through the EXISTING actionRegistry (listViewDefinition.js already accepted rowActions ids and nothing consumed them -- a fourth unconsumed declaration); action activation cannot trigger row navigation (propagation stopped at the actions cell, Enter/Space handled explicitly after confirming jsdom does not synthesise a click from keydown); focus redirects to the list container when an action removes its own focused row; a denied action renders visible+disabled with its reason, because a hidden action reads as 'no actions exist'. Integration added the missing CSS for the class hooks the grid ships.

entries.title: Contacts and Locations wired through metadata
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: Both wired, nothing declined, no accessibility regression. Deliberately did NOT use DefaultRelatedList's default binding, which issues its own live read while AccountDetail already runs useContactsForAccount/useLocationsForAccount -- that would have re-read both collections, the recorded #1094/#1095 double-read anti-pattern. An injected listRenderer builds the presentation model from the data already flowing, keeping the shared grid, the four states and the focus handoff without a second subscription. The focus-parity proof initially gave a FALSE PASS -- a fresh render() reset component state -- and the lane caught that itself and switched to rerender, which is the only reason the test means anything. account.locations was CHECKED rather than assumed and does exist, so the older recorded gap was already closed. Location's nested address map vs flat addressCity/addressState field ids was found by trying and flattened. Section-level add/import affordances stay hand-mounted; the grid has no equivalent, stated rather than dropped.

entries.title: cellValue() had no BOOLEAN branch -- boolean columns rendered blank either way
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: The SEVENTH instance of the unconsumed-declaration pattern and the second of its exact kind: a declared field type with no rendering branch, after TIMESTAMP. React renders neither true nor false as a child, so contact.isPrimary came out BLANK on every row -- primary and non-primary indistinguishable. The leaf lane worked around it locally by pre-mapping to 'Primary'/null; at integration the fix was moved to cellValue and the workaround REMOVED, the same call as the stale rowNavigationTo in #1207. It would also have broken outright, since pre-mapping a BOOLEAN to a string is now coerced by the branch that fixed it. Renders the app's established Yes/No. A genuinely absent value still renders nothing, and a non-primary contact now reads 'No' rather than blank: 'is not the primary' and 'nobody recorded whether they are' are different claims, and a blank cell says neither.

entries.title: Audit of every declared FIELD_TYPE against cellValue's branches
entries.nextAction: None. Findings split into the three entries below.
entries.notes: Run deliberately after BOOLEAN became the second field type found missing a renderer branch, rather than waiting for a wiring lane to find the next one by accident. entityDefinition.js declares eleven FIELD_TYPEs; cellValue resolves five (ENUM, ENUM_SET, TIMESTAMP, DATE, BOOLEAN) and returns the raw stored value for the rest. STRING/TEXT/NUMBER are correct raw. The remainder are not, and every one is latent only because the declaring list is not yet wired to a surface -- which is precisely the next wave of work. Method: enumerate every column of every real list definition, resolve its declared field type from the owning entity, and compare against the branches cellValue actually implements.

entries.title: REFERENCE columns render the raw document id -- ten of them across the repo
entries.nextAction: Supply a real resolveReference when an INDEX surface is wired.
entries.notes: Ten REFERENCE columns are declared across contact, equipment (x2), invoice, location, opportunity, purchaseOrder, salesOrder, truck and workOrder index lists. cellValue has no REFERENCE branch, so each would render the raw stored document id as cell content -- the exact defect DECISIONS #106 exists to prevent, in the exact place the program has been removing it from hand-written surfaces. Unlike BOOLEAN or TIMESTAMP this is NOT a formatting fix: rendering a reference honestly means resolving it to the target's human-meaningful value, which needs a read the presentation layer does not have. The options are a denormalized display field on the source record (equipmentModel already does this with manufacturerName), a resolver injected into the presentation build, or refusing REFERENCE as a column type. Latent today only because none of these lists is wired. RESOLVED by an injected resolveReference(fieldId, id, row) threaded through buildListPresentation. The decision was ALREADY IN THE REPO: every one of the ten REFERENCE fields carries the same field comment, 'Display resolution belongs to the [target] entity, not to this field' -- written independently ten times, which rules out the denormalized-field option directly (no sibling display field exists or is invited for any of them, in deliberate contrast to equipmentModel.js's genuine manufacturerName). None of the ten should be removed; all are legitimate columns. Unresolvable renders 'Unresolved reference', the SAME state whether no resolver was supplied or the resolver returned nothing, since to a reader both mean the same thing; a genuinely UNSET reference still renders blank, keeping 'nothing is linked' and 'something is linked and I could not show it' distinct. MetadataRecordPage's FieldGroup shares cellValue and was fixed for free -- it would have leaked a raw id for any REFERENCE field reaching it. VERIFIED before merge that no live surface regressed: only INDEX lists declare REFERENCE columns, and the wired Account page uses RELATED lists.

entries.title: CURRENCY_MINOR renders minor units, and invoice.dueDate is typed NUMBER
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: Two mechanical defects, both currently latent. (1) invoice.totalMinor and invoice.outstandingMinor are CURRENCY_MINOR -- integer minor units by contract -- and cellValue returns them raw, so a $125.00 invoice would display as 12500. Money wrong by a factor of one hundred is not a formatting nicety. (2) invoice.dueDate is declared NUMBER and its own description says 'Ms epoch, carried at issuance' -- so a due date would render as 1755993600000. formatTimestamp already coerces epoch millis, so the honest fix is the declared type, not a special case: the field IS a date and says so in prose while claiming to be a number. RESOLVED. CURRENCY_MINOR now formats through formatMinor (domain/accountArView.js), already the consumed formatter for outstandingMinor on the Account AR panel, with currency read from the row's own currency field per the sibling-field contract rather than a hardcoded symbol. Zero renders 0.00 and absent renders nothing -- a zero balance and an unknown balance are different claims. dueDate retyped NUMBER->DATE, with requiredIndexes() re-run to confirm the demand set stays empty (no declared filter, not in default sort).

entries.title: Two money formatters disagree on non-2-exponent currencies
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: domain/money.js's formatMoneyMajor respects currencyExponent; domain/accountArView.js's formatMinor hardcodes division by 100. They disagree for any currency whose minor unit is not 1/100 -- JPY being the obvious case. formatMoneyMajor takes a {minor,currency} value object and has ZERO call sites anywhere in the app; formatMinor is the one actually consumed. The lane reused the consumed one and REPORTED the conflict rather than silently choosing, which is correct. This is the second time in one session two formatters have been found answering the same question differently (see also the displayTimestamp vs accountPortfolio.formatLastUpdate overlap recorded under A-LIST-TIMESTAMP-AND-NAVIGATION). Worth deciding deliberately: either reconcile them, or record that this system is 2-exponent-only and delete the unused one -- an unused formatter that disagrees with the used one is a trap for whoever reaches for it next. RESOLVED, and the lane REVERSED the option I leaned toward. I suggested that if the system is USD-only, the right move was to record the constraint and delete the divergent formatter. The lane established that USD-only is a fact of the WRITE PATHS, not of the SCHEMA -- salesOrderCommands.ts hardcodes USD and every downstream command fail-closes against it with CURRENCY_MISMATCH, but account.defaultCurrency is validated against the full ISO 4217 set including JPY, and salesOrderCommands.ts's own comment names multi-currency as a future seam. So /100 was a live defect waiting on a seam that already exists in the data model, and deleting the CORRECT implementation would have made the trap permanent and invisible. Instead formatMinorUnits became the single exponent-aware core with both prior names delegating to it; no call signature changed, so listPresentation.js needed no edit at all. No USD output changed.

entries.title: manufacturerIndexList declares the document id as a visible column
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: manufacturer.js declares manufacturerId (type ID, described as 'the Firestore document id, also written into the document body') as a COLUMN in manufacturerIndexList. manufacturerEntity declares neither a nameField nor a referenceField. That combination is the precise failure DECISIONS #106 names: a missing business reference is not permission to display a record id. The id is very likely in the column list BECAUSE nothing else was declared to identify the record, which is the rationalisation the rule exists to refuse. Needs the real human-meaningful field established from storage, not an invented one. CORRECTION -- this entry as originally written was WRONG on a load-bearing point. It claimed manufacturerEntity declares neither a nameField nor a referenceField. It DOES declare identity.nameField 'name'; my audit probe read .nameField at the top level of the entity and found nothing there. referenceField: null is correct and deliberate -- no reference number exists in the write path and none was invented. So the defect was narrower and plainer than recorded: a human-meaningful name was already declared and the document id was in the visible column list anyway. The rationalisation I attributed to it ('the id is there because nothing else identifies the record') did not apply. RESOLVED by removing the id column.

entries.title: validateRegistryReferences is never run over real definitions
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: resolveRowActions in MetadataRecordPage.jsx silently drops an unregistered action id, justified as matching validateRegistryReferences' philosophy. That validator DOES check rowActions -- but its only caller anywhere in the repo is its own unit test, so no real definition is ever validated by it. The justification therefore does not hold and an unregistered id would vanish with no trace. Not patched blind: wiring the validator over real definitions depends on when the component/action registries are populated, and a node test against empty registries would fail for the wrong reason. RESOLVED. Two checks, both honestly scoped: all 20 real ListViewDefinitions validated in the node:test suite already wired to CI, and accountRecordPage validated against the GENUINELY populated registry by driving the real registerAccountPageComponents(). The lane explicitly avoided a hand-built registry, which would have recreated the hollow assurance this item exists to remove, and states plainly in the test file that the list-definition check is currently VACUOUS -- no real list definition declares a renderer or row action yet, so it is a forward tripwire rather than present-day coverage. Both checks were proved to FAIL on a bogus reference before being reverted.

entries.title: pageRegistryReferences was also unconsumed -- and the wrong validator passes silently
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: The SIXTH instance of the unconsumed-declaration pattern, and the most dangerous shape of it so far. pageRegistryReferences (pageDefinition.js) is the correctly-shaped sibling for PageDefinitions and also had no caller but its own unit test. The trap: validateRegistryReferences reads the ListViewDefinition shape (.columns/.rowActions), while a PageDefinition keeps its references in .sections[].componentId and .headerActions -- so calling the well-known validator on a real page definition finds ZERO references and PASSES. A green check that proves nothing is worse than no check, and a naive fix to X-REGISTRY-VALIDATOR-NEVER-RUN would have produced exactly that.

entries.title: actionRegistry.register() is never called in application source
entries.nextAction: Register real actions when a definition first declares one; until then rowActions is inert.
entries.notes: actionRegistry.register() is called nowhere in src/ -- only in test files -- so the action side of the registry is structurally empty in production. Harmless today only because no definition declares an action id, which also means the rowActions path shipped in #1211 is INERT in production until something registers one. Recorded rather than absorbed: this is the same pattern in its mirror image -- not a declaration nobody reads, but a reader nobody feeds.

entries.title: Metadata declares things nothing reads -- seven instances in one session
entries.nextAction: None. Recorded as a program-level pattern to check for, not a single defect.
entries.notes: Four instances surfaced within one session, each found by trying to USE the metadata rather than by reading it: (1) readVia declared and ignored by the RELATED_LIST binding, which would have reported every viewer as denied; (2) rowNavigationTo declared by every list definition and read by nothing, hiding a route that had never existed and would have 404'd every row the instant it was consumed; (3) rowActions ids accepted by listViewDefinition.js and consumed by nothing; (4) validateRegistryReferences itself, never run over a real definition. capabilityParts was nearly the fifth and was deliberately gated instead. The common shape: a declaration is harmless while unread, so it is never wrong, so it is never corrected -- and it fails the moment something finally reads it. The detection method that worked every time was attempting to consume the declaration honestly; none was found by review. UPDATED: two further instances found after this entry was written. (5) pageRegistryReferences, unconsumed AND shadowed by a similarly-named validator that silently passes on the wrong shape -- see X-PAGE-REGISTRY-REFERENCES-UNCONSUMED. (6) actionRegistry, the mirror image: not a declaration nobody reads but a reader nobody feeds. The detection method held for every one of them -- each was found by attempting to consume the declaration honestly, none by review. (7) cellValue had no BOOLEAN branch -- see X-LIST-BOOLEAN-FORMATTING. Note the sub-pattern now visible across TIMESTAMP and BOOLEAN: entityDefinition.js declares a field-type vocabulary that the renderer implements only PARTLY, and the unimplemented members fail silently rather than loudly. Worth auditing the remaining declared types against cellValue's branches before the next wiring lane finds the eighth by accident. (8) resolveReference, introduced by #1221 with no caller supplying it -- and the FIRST instance of this pattern that is acceptable, for exactly one reason: it is LOUD. An unsupplied resolver renders 'Unresolved reference' in the cell. Every previous instance was SILENT -- a blank cell, a raw id, a route to a 404, a check that checked nothing -- which is why each survived until something finally consumed it. The distinction to carry forward is not 'never leave a seam unconsumed'; it is 'an unconsumed seam must announce itself'. A loud seam is a TODO. A silent one is a defect waiting for a date.

entries.title: origin/main went red: #1204 merged without rebasing onto #1202
entries.nextAction: None. Recorded as an integration-practice finding.
entries.notes: MY error as integration lane, not a lane's. #1204 was based on 160587b7, which predates #1202 (d2b69427) and therefore predates accountPageComponents.test.jsx. Both PRs were green on their own bases and semantically incompatible once combined -- git had no textual conflict to report. #1204 made DefaultRelatedList call useNavigate() unconditionally, so every render reaching it needs Router context; the lane REPORTED exactly this and wrapped the renders it could see, but could not see a file that did not exist on its base. Two of the four failures were #1202's BLOCKER tests asserting the defects still existed -- #1204 fixed them, so they inverted rather than got wrapped, which is precisely what those tests were for. LESSON: a leaf handoff verified against ITS OWN base is not sufficient; the integration lane must re-run the suite on a base containing every PR being combined. Recorded so the practice changes, not just the file.

entries.title: opportunity.js declared a rowNavigationTo route that never existed
entries.nextAction: Restore a rowNavigationTo only when a real per-Opportunity route exists.
entries.notes: opportunity.js declared rowNavigationTo '/sales/opportunities/:id' on both its index and related lists. No such route has ever existed in App.jsx -- the only Opportunity route is the workspace at /customers/opportunities, which takes no :id. It survived only because nothing consumed rowNavigationTo; the moment A-LIST-TIMESTAMP-AND-NAVIGATION made the runtime read it, every Opportunity row would have linked to a 404. This is the direct cost of a declaration with no consumer: it is never wrong until it suddenly is. The wiring lane correctly stripped it within its own scope and reported the file as REGISTRATION_PENDING; at integration the declaration was REMOVED from opportunity.js and the workaround dropped, because a consumer defending against a bad declaration leaves it in place for the next consumer. Pinned at the definition so the truth is inherited rather than re-litigated.

entries.title: Inventory Transaction has neither a name nor a reference -- definition held, not merged
entries.nextAction: Owner decision: do inventory movements get a business reference, or is the ledger unlabelable?
entries.notes: The authored definition is COMPLETE and preserved on its branch; it is not merged, on the same precedent as X-TRANSFER-ORDER-NO-REFERENCE and X-SALES-ORDER-NO-REFERENCE. The lane declared identity.nameField 'type' and flagged it honestly as the least-invented option, because validateEntityDefinition rejects an entity with neither. But `type` is an ENUM CATEGORY -- every RECEIVED movement would label as 'RECEIVED' and the rows would be mutually indistinguishable. The validator's own message settles it: an entity with neither 'cannot be labelled without exposing its document id, which is a data-model gap to RECORD, not a fallback to NORMALIZE'. Passing the validator by nominating a category IS that normalization, so merging would have made the contract weaker than the comment inside it. This is the first entity in the program with genuinely no labelable identity. Other findings from the same lane, preserved: inventory_transactions is genuinely append-only with two disjoint stored shapes (legacy `timestamp` only, no actor at all; operational `actor{kind,id}` + server-authored `recordedAt`), which is also why no INDEX list was authored -- no field is sortable across both eras without silently dropping one. And `lotId` is a legal stored key required when a Part's trackingMode is LOT that NO live writer populates, so a LOT-tracked movement would fail validation today.

blockers.reason: inventory_transactions has neither a human name nor a server-allocated reference. The authored definition satisfies the validator only by nominating `type`, an ENUM category that would label every RECEIVED movement identically -- the exact normalization entityDefinition.js forbids.
blockers.requiredDecision: Does an inventory movement get a business reference number (a family member alongside WO-/OPP-/SO-), or is this ledger accepted as an unlabelable internal record that no surface may list by identity? Numbering is a business decision outside a leaf lane's authority.

entries.title: cellValue() has no TIMESTAMP branch -- a date column renders as an epoch number
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: listPresentation.js resolves ENUM and ENUM_SET through their label maps but has no TIMESTAMP or DATE branch anywhere in the repo, so a declared TIMESTAMP column renders the stored value directly. That is a machine value reaching a user -- the same class of defect enum resolution exists to prevent, one type over. entries.title: rowNavigationTo is declared by every list definition and consumed by nothing
entries.nextAction: None.
entries.notes: makeListViewDefinition accepts rowNavigationTo as a route template and nothing in src/ reads it -- confirmed by repo-wide search, the sole hit is its own declaration. DefaultRelatedList passes MetadataListGrid no onRowClick, so metadata-rendered rows are inert. Wiring Sales Orders would therefore have discarded a real, currently-working per-order route. This is the same shape of problem as the readVia gap: metadata declaring something the runtime silently ignores. The document id must remain a ROUTING key -- it may reach a URL, never a cell.
